events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.87)
events.body:
The ride was a fixed-quote RydeX trip from NUS to Raffles Place, $24.64, pickup 08:36 and drop-off 08:51 [F1]. The rider's complaint alleges speeding, hard braking the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder and that she felt scared and unsafe; that is a dangerous-driving allegation and SAFE-2 requires the case to be routed to a person rather than decided automatically. The trace confirms the screen has already marked this as a safety incident, so escalate is the only available outcome [F1][F2][SAFE-2].

The measurable records do not settle the allegation either way: the driven distance was 10.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route (-0.1 km) and the trip took 15.9 min against a 16.5 min estimate [F1][F2]. Those aggregates are consistent with ordinary driving and show no off-route segment, so no route-deviation refund arises and no fare element is recoverable; but they record no speed profile, no braking events and no lane or shoulder information, so they cannot exclude brief speeding or hard braking inside an otherwise on-time trip. That gap is exactly why SAFE-2 sends the matter to a human [F1][F2][RD-1][SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

On the second safety element, reading F6 in context: the driver's post-trip statement says "The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip. I drove normally." The words "stupid" and the phone accusation are hostile remarks aimed at the rider; under Ryde's Code of Conduct, which bars abuse of any kind, and reading the words themselves rather than a keyword, this is at least a suspected abuse-of-the-rider issue for the reviewer to assess under SAFE-1, and it also conflicts with the complete, fully timestamped chat record, which shows only the pickup arrangement and no mention of phone use [F3][F4][F5][F6][SAFE-1]. I do not decide it here; the record goes to a person.

The chat contains no contemporaneous report of dangerous driving during the ride, and no traffic facts exist to corroborate or rebut the allegation; I treat the absence of corroboration as a gap, not as evidence for the driver [F3][F4][F5][SAFE-2]. Since neither party's profile may decide the case and neither party has a record of repeated violations, no account flag attaches to either side [F7][F8][RD-6]. The fare is a fixed RydeX quote with no challenged add-on, so nothing monetary is ordered and the amount is left null [F1][FARE-1].

claims.assertion: The rider's complaint is a dangerous-driving allegation ('speeding and braking hard the whole way, overtaking on the shoulder. I was scared and felt unsafe'), which is expressly within SAFE-2; the case must go to a human and no automated ruling on the fare should be issued.

The driver's written statement calls the rider 'stupid' ('The rider is stupid and was on the phone the whole trip'), an abusive remark recorded in the ride record; the judge should read the original words and, if found abusive, treat it under SAFE-1 and escalate to a person.

The rider's description of being frightened and feeling unsafe, together with the driver's abusive written statement, means the record contains a safety concern that must be recorded and routed to human handling rather than decided automatically.

The GPS record shows no route deviation (actual 10.5 km vs optimal 10.6 km, -0.1 km / -1%) and no off-route segment, so this case involves no fare overcharge to recover and the requested outcome is limited to escalation for the safety allegation.

Both the rider (4.8 rating, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d) and the driver (4.78 rating, 0 disputes / 0 upheld in 90 d) have clean dispute histories, so no flag_account action against either party is supported on this record.

weaknesses: The only safety evidence is the rider's own complaint narrative; the chat record (F3, F4) contains no contemporaneous message from the rider reporting speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking during the trip, and the driver's statement (F6) denies it ('I drove normally').

The system records contradict the notion of any abnormal driving pattern in the measurable dimension: F1 shows the route was actually shorter than optimal and F2 shows the trip finished 0.6 min earlier than the estimate, which the other side will use to argue the ride was ordinary.
There are no traffic or weather facts in this case (the traffic slice is empty), so no external record corroborates or rebuts hard braking or shoulder overtaking.

The driver's 'stupid and was on the phone' remark (F6) is insulting but contains no threat or intimidation wording, so the other side may argue it does not meet the SAFE-1 threshold and only warrants general handling.

claims.assertion: This is a dangerous-driving complaint (speeding, hard braking, overtaking on the shoulder), i.e. an allegation of a traffic-safety nature; the record contains no charge or adverse finding of any kind, and the complaint rests entirely on the rider's recollection with no telematics or video corroboration in the fact table.

The only objective route record shows the trip was driven 10.5 km against a 10.6 km optimal route (-0.1 km, -1%) — shorter than optimal — with no off-route segment recorded, so the ride took the shortest and most direct route rather than any elongated or erratic path (RD-1).

The trip completed in 15.9 minutes against a 16.5-minute estimate (-0.6 min), i.e. slightly faster than predicted door-to-door; that is consistent with normal efficient driving and provides no support for sustained speeding, since no segment of the record exceeds the estimate.

The chat record is complete and fully timestamped (2 messages, all timestamped) and contains only the pickup arrangement — the rider's 'I am outside University Hall' and the driver's 'about 6 min, blue Toyota Prius' — with no complaint, safety concern or request to slow down raised at any point during or after the trip.

The driver's written statement contains an insult directed at the rider ('The rider is stupid'), which is discourteous but is not a threat, intimidation, harassment or physical-attack statement within the meaning of the safety clause; the policy's excluded conduct is assault, harassment, abuse, threats and unwanted advances, and the rider's own complaint alleges no such conduct by the driver.

The driver's record is clean: 3.9 years on the platform, 4.78 rating over 705 trips in the last 90 days, with 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes; there is no pattern of safety, route or conduct violations to support any account action against the driver.

The fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $24.64 and no additional charge, waiting fee, cancellation fee or unexplained item appears in the complaint or the record, so there is nothing monetary to refund and the fare must stand unchanged.

weaknesses: The rider's complaint is a first-hand account of feeling scared by speeding, hard braking and shoulder overtaking; the driver cannot disprove the rider's subjective experience and the GPS/timeline record (F1, F2) is only aggregate distance and duration — it records no speed profile, no harsh-braking event and no lane/shoulder data, so it cannot affirmatively exclude a brief burst of speeding within an otherwise on-time trip.

The driver's own written statement (F6) is hostile and calls the rider 'stupid'; the other side will use it to argue the driver's account of 'I drove normally' is not credible and that the rider's fear was reasonable.

The rider's profile (F7) is clean — 4.0 years, 4.8 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days — so the rider has no history of vexatious safety complaints, which weakens any suggestion the complaint is fabricated.

Because the complaint is a safety allegation, SAFE-1/SAFE-2 screening can send the whole case to a human reviewer regardless of how weak the evidence is (F6 is the natural trigger), so the driver cannot obtain a clean no-action ruling from this forum alone.

points.response: Conceded as to the nature of the case: D1 is right that this is a safety allegation, but that conclusion runs against the driver, not for him — under SAFE-2 such a case is not decided automatically at all, so the driver's requested no_action is not an available outcome on this record.

D2 is irrelevant to the rider's complaint: F1 establishes only that no fare deviation is claimed, and it says nothing about speed, braking or shoulder use, which is exactly what the rider reported; the absence of an off-route segment cannot answer a dangerous-driving allegation.

F2 shows only that the door-to-door time was 0.6 min under the estimate; an on-time aggregate duration cannot exclude bursts of speeding and hard braking within the trip, and the driver's own admission confirms the record contains no speed profile (F1, F2).

The completeness of the chat record (F5) cuts the other way for the driver: the chat contains only two messages (F3, F4) and nothing in it corroborates the driver's assertion in F6 that the rider 'was on the phone the whole trip' — a contradicting claim under system-record primacy.

Whether F6's 'The rider is stupid' is abusive is for the judge to read, not for the driver to characterise; the policy text lists 'abuse of any kind' among unacceptable conduct, and combined with the rider's fear complaint it is a proper trigger for human handling under SAFE-1.

F8 shows a clean dispute history, which is why we do not seek flag_account against the driver; it does not bear on whether an unrecorded dangerous-driving incident occurred, and profile facts may never decide the case.
Not contested — the fare is a fixed RydeX quote and the rider seeks no money; the requested outcome is escalation of the safety allegation only, not any refund.

I do not contest that a dangerous-driving allegation falls within SAFE-2 and that this forum cannot try it; but the same clause sends the case to a person without any finding of fault, and nothing in the system record corroborates the allegation — F1 shows a route 0.1 km shorter than optimal and F2 a trip 0.6 min faster than the 16.5-min estimate, an unremarkable profile. I therefore ask that the escalation be recorded as an open, unproven allegation and that the fare of $24.64 remain unchanged.

The insult in F6 ('The rider is stupid') is a discourtesy, not a threat, intimidation or harassment: it names no consequence, no violence and no unwanted advance, and the driver's own account in the same sentence is 'I drove normally'. SAFE-1 turns on assault, harassment, abuse, threats and unwanted advances, so the words should be read and, if the reviewer regards them as abusive, handled toward the driver, but they cannot by themselves carry a finding that the rider's driving complaint is true.

There is no safety concern recorded anywhere except the rider's post-hoc narrative: the complete, fully timestamped chat record (F5) contains only F3 ("I am outside University Hall, in a blue shirt") and F4 (the driver's ETA reply) and not one message reporting speeding, hard braking or shoulder overtaking during the ride. Per the system-records-first rule the aggregate GPS record, which shows no abnormality (F1, F2), is the better evidence, so escalation should produce no adverse finding in place of the missing proof.

Agreed — F1 records no off-route segment and no excess distance (10.5 km vs 10.6 km optimal), F2 shows the trip was not prolonged (15.9 min vs 16.5 min), and the fare was a fixed RydeX quote of $24.64 with no challenged add-on; I withdraw nothing on my side and confirm there is no fare overcharge to refund under FARE-1/RD-2.

Agreed, and this cuts only one way for my client: F8 shows 3.9 years, 4.78 rating, 705 trips in 90 days with 0 disputes and 0 upheld, so there is no 'repeated' violation and no basis for any account action against the driver; the rider's clean history (F7) likewise supports no action against her.

I do not withdraw D1; the point stands that the complaint rests on recollection alone, and I add only that the single objective record produced by this case (F1, F2) is neutral-to-favourable to the driver, which is why the escalation should close without a fault finding against him.
